close_reason: Clippy passes clean. Manual matches are correct and explicit; combinator rewrite adds no safety/correctness benefit here. Closing as opinion.
description: Throughout submission.rs, mailbox.rs, email.rs, identity.rs, vacation.rs the pattern 'match x { Some(v) => v.clone(), None => continue }' and 'match x { Some(s) => s, None => continue }' appears repeatedly. The idiomatic form in context (especially for Option<String>) is .ok_or_else(...)? or if let/continue patterns using the ? operator where possible. Specifically: (1) In vacation.rs get handler line 31-37, 'requested_ids: Option<Vec<String>>' is fetched by cloning the Value then deserialized — the ids field is a JSON array of strings that could be parsed without clone using v.as_array() iteration. (2) In submission.rs process_create line 709-718, .ok_or_else() is used correctly, but the code repeating the same structure for identityId and emailId could be a helper. These are clippy-level style issues — the code is correct — but the clone-heavy pattern signals the author was avoiding borrow checker friction rather than structuring to avoid it.
title: Pervasive manual match on Option where combinators suffice
